only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] Intestinal crypt epithelium maintained by Wnt signalling is what these genes describe: a stem and progenitor programme of the colonic crypt base together with markers of the differentiating epithelium above it. It sustains the continuous renewal of the gut lining, and its inappropriate reactivation underlies colorectal adenoma and carcinoma, where the same transcripts serve as tumour markers.

[untitled BTM module] These genes define the differentiated intestinal epithelium, the absorptive lineage that lines the small bowel and colon and carries out nutrient uptake, barrier maintenance and fluid balance. The programme is set by a transcription factor core in which CDX1 and CDX2 specify intestinal identity and HNF4A and HNF4G drive enterocyte maturation; loss or ectopic activation of these factors underlies intestinal metaplasia and is used to distinguish gut-derived tumours.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the differentiated absorptive and secretory epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract, the barrier layer that absorbs nutrients, detoxifies luminal xenobiotics and presents a glycan-coated surface to the microbiota. Adhesion and junctional components such as EPCAM and FERMT1 hold the sheet together, while lineage transcription factors including FOXA3 and KLF5 drive and maintain the differentiated state; loss of these programmes underlies barrier failure, inflammatory bowel disease and the dedifferentiation seen in colorectal cancer, where CEACAM and galectin-4 expression is routinely used as an epithelial marker.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the differentiated intestinal and hepatic epithelium and the transcriptional programme that specifies it. HNF4A and HNF4G, with FOXA3, act as master regulators of enterocyte and hepatocyte identity, driving expression of the brush-border and junctional machinery that makes an absorptive epithelium possible: villin as the microvillar actin-bundling protein, claudin-2 setting paracellular cation and water permeability in the proximal intestine, and harmonin (USH1C) organising apical scaffolds.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the epithelial identity programme of stratified and glandular epithelia, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract, and its coordinated regulation of differentiation, adhesion and mucosal barrier function. Transcription factors set the programme: CDX1 specifies intestinal identity and is a determinant of intestinal metaplasia when expressed in stomach or oesophagus, while KLF5 and the ETS factor EHF drive proliferation and maturation of epithelial progenitors.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the transcriptional and structural programme that gives absorptive epithelium of the gut and kidney tubule its identity: a polarized brush-border cell that moves solutes across a sealed barrier. HNF4G, TFAP2C and SIX4 act as lineage-directing transcription factors, while CLDN2 builds a cation- and water-permeable tight junction pore that sets paracellular leakiness, and SLC3A1 supplies the heavy subunit of the transporter that reabsorbs cystine and dibasic amino acids — its loss causes cystinuria with kidney stones.

[untitled BTM module] These genes together mark the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine, the cell layer that takes up nutrients, senses dietary and xenobiotic chemicals, and forms a barrier to gut contents. Lineage-defining transcription factors such as CDX1 and HNF4G impose regional intestinal identity on gut endoderm and drive expression of the enterocyte's working machinery: a brush border built with the unconventional myosin MYO1A, apical solute carriers including SLC3A1 for cystine and dibasic amino acids and the zinc transporter SLC39A5, and HMGCS2 for ketogenesis from fatty acids in a tissue with high energetic turnover.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine and liver, the tissue that takes up nutrients, forms a selective barrier, and performs first-pass metabolism of drugs and dietary xenobiotics. Its identity is set transcriptionally by the nuclear receptors HNF4A and HNF4G, which drive expression of brush border and apical junction components such as villin, CDHR5 and the harmonin scaffold USH1C, together with the lectin LGALS4 and the tetraspanin-like TM4SF5.

members: [untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation.

only_in_theme: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the erythroid-megakaryocytic branch of hematopoiesis, the programme by which bone marrow progenitors commit to making red cells and platelets rather than lymphoid or granulocytic fates. Its transcriptional core is a TAL1-GFI1B axis that drives erythroid gene expression while restraining progenitor proliferation; loss of either blocks red cell production, and GFI1B mutation causes a bleeding disorder with malformed platelets.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the transcriptional programme of immature myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow, the stage at which granulocyte, mast cell and erythroid potential is still being resolved and primary granule proteins are first made. Its hallmark products are the azurophilic granule enzymes myeloperoxidase and neutrophil elastase, together with the mast cell protease carboxypeptidase A3 and the promyelocyte membrane marker MS4A3, so the signature marks promyelocytes and their close relatives rather than mature blood cells.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation.
only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] The genes here sketch late erythroid differentiation and the assembly of the red cell surface. Erythropoiesis matters because it supplies the circulating oxygen carriers, and its transcriptional and membrane components determine both red cell mechanical resilience and the antigens that decide transfusion compatibility.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. Its recognisable core is the kinase TAK1 (MAP3K7) acting upstream of the CREB/ATF family factors ATF1 and ATF2, a route by which cytokine, TGF-beta and stress inputs are converted into changes in gene expression governing inflammation, survival and differentiation; loss of TAK1 signalling causes inflammatory and developmental failure.
